title: H2054 (191st General Court): Relative to the lawful sale of ammunition

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check); operative text read by source-collector (Sonnet) from the saved official copy

operative_text:
Sec. 1 (amending G.L. c. 140 s. 23): Notwithstanding any special law or regulation to the contrary nothing in this section shall be deemed as requiring a company outside of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts to be required to be licensed under this section. Said companies shall be entitled to sell and deliver inert ammunition components to persons properly licensed to possess or purchase ammunition under sections, 129B or 131 of this chapter, through the internet, U.S. Mail or by any other means common to interstate commerce. All deliveries of ammunition under this paragraph, whether in person or by common carrier, must require the signature of the licensee and photographic identification.
Sec. 1 (amending G.L. c. 140 s. 23): For the purposes of this section the term "inert components" shall include, but not be limited to the following: cases, bullets, shot, wads.
